record.what_it_does: Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento) is a self-hosted or cloud-hosted ecommerce platform that exposes REST, GraphQL, and SOAP web APIs for managing catalog, orders, customers, carts, and other store objects.
record.auth_primary: Other (OAuth 1.0a) for third-party integrations; Bearer admin/integration/customer tokens for simpler cases
record.auth_notes: Adobe Commerce/Magento documents three authentication paths: (1) OAuth 1.0a for third-party applications (the recommended path for external integrations), (2) token-based Bearer auth where Admin/Customer/Integration tokens are requested via login endpoints and sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (integration tokens can optionally be used standalone as never-expiring bearer tokens if an admin enables that setting), and (3) session/login credential auth for Admin and Customer users. On Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS), there is also an IMS (Adobe Identity Management System) OAuth2-based access-token flow for web API calls. Credentials are always issued per-store by a store admin creating an 'Integration' in the Magento Admin panel — there is no vendor-wide multi-tenant OAuth app registry.
record.access_notes: Magento Open Source is free to download and self-host, and a developer can spin up a local/sandbox instance, create an Integration in the Admin panel, and get working OAuth 1.0a or Bearer credentials immediately at no cost. Adobe Commerce (the SaaS/PaaS enterprise edition, which adds the IMS auth flow, webhooks-as-a-service, etc.) requires a paid commercial license/contract — there is no free signup for that tier. Either way, credentials are issued per merchant instance by that instance's own admin, not through a central developer portal.
record.main_blocker: No centralized multi-tenant OAuth app model — each merchant's self-hosted/cloud instance requires its own admin to manually create an Integration and issue OAuth 1.0a or Bearer credentials, so a multi-user agent toolkit needs a per-customer setup flow rather than a single vendor OAuth app.

record.open_questions: The official Adobe MCP servers found (App Builder MCP, dropins MCP) are aimed at IDE/development-time assistance (docs lookup, App Builder scaffolding, storefront drop-in data) rather than exposing Commerce REST/GraphQL operations (orders, products, customers) as callable agent tools — unclear if any official MCP directly proxies transactional Commerce API actions for end-user agents. Also unclear whether Adobe Commerce SaaS's IMS OAuth2 flow is available to arbitrary third-party developers or only to the merchant's own admin-integrated apps.
